clue.text: US politician about to meet innkeeper

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
a publican runs a pub, an inn

explanation.surface: An American politician is about to have a meeting with the landlord of a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A Republican is a member of one of the two major parties in American politics.

clue.text: Tear shed for exploitation

parts.note: to rip is to tear
shed means removed, off, as in clothes taken off

explanation.surface: Crying in the cowshed, or ripping down a shed, for profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rip-off is a swindle or overcharge, taking unfair advantage of a buyer.

clue.text: Favouring healthy yield

parts.note: pro means in favour of
fit means in good health

explanation.surface: A sound investment providing a good return.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is the gain or return from an investment, its yield.

clue.text: He joins the family after the match

definitions.text: He joins the family after the match

parts.words: He joins the family after the match
parts.note: the match is a marriage, not a sporting fixture, so this is a man who becomes a relative by a wedding

explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a game; here it is a marriage, after which a sister's husband becomes a relation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister's husband becomes kin through the wedding, an in-law relation.

clue.text: Wild beast regularly ignored important date in March

indicators.note: every other letter is skipped, leaving the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A wild animal on the loose takes no notice of a key day in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides of March, the fifteenth, is the day Julius Caesar was assassinated.

clue.text: Novel getting fan mail sorted by member

indicators.note: by means next to, so the limb follows
sorted means the letters are put into a different order

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A book receives fan mail that a member of staff sorts out.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal Farm is George Orwell's 1945 allegorical tale of revolution, a famous book.

clue.text: Joint enterprise in prison

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ..., a cooperative business owned jointly by its members
second meaning: ... is slang for a jail, somewhere one is ... up

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the Co-op is also a familiar chain of shops run as a cooperative.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooperative is a business shared by its members, and a coop is a pen or cage, hence slang for jail.

clue.text: Old boss to stock new shrub

indicators.note: to stock means to hold inside, so the boss contains the next piece

parts.note: a leader is a boss

explanation.surface: A retired manager has to stock a new plant in a nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is a poisonous evergreen Mediterranean bush with pink or white flowers.

clue.text: Bolshie traveller coming up with lines

indicators.note: in a down entry coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is a commercial traveller
verse is lines of poetry

explanation.surface: A difficult salesman arrives with lines of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshie is British slang for awkward and contrary, deliberately uncooperative, i.e. perverse.

clue.text: Striking new 6 in the centre of Wigan

indicators.note: new tells us to make something fresh out of the letters that follow

parts.note: the answer to 6 across, the joint enterprise

indicators.note: the middle letter of a five-letter word is its centre

parts.note: Wigan is a town in Lancashire, England; its central letter is taken

explanation.surface: Something remarkable and newly built sits at the heart of the town of Wigan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges COOP (the answer to 6 across) with IN, THE and G, the middle letter of Wigan.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone photogenic looks striking in pictures, attractive on camera.

clue.text: Clothes deteriorate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... is clothing, as in evening ...
second meaning: to be worn down by use

explanation.definitionFit: Wear names garments of a kind (menswear) and, as a verb, gradual damage from use, as in wear thin.

clue.text: Only nude Berg production at this opera house

indicators.note: a production is a staging, so the letters are put on in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An opera house staging only nude productions of Berg, the composer of Wozzeck and Lulu.
explanation.definitionFit: Glyndebourne is a country house in Sussex, England, famous for its summer opera festival.

clue.text: Not finding last of baggage in cargo causes alarm

indicators.note: not finding a letter means it is absent from the word for cargo

parts.note: freight is goods carried as cargo

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is the one taken

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: Luggage goes missing from the hold, which worries the travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not finding' removes E, the last letter of baggage, from FREIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden scare, a synonym of alarm as a noun.

clue.text: Cut after cut cut, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: after places the first word's letters behind the second's
the third cut says the word before it is itself cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim
to lance is to cut open with a blade

explanation.surface: A repeated stammer of the word cut, framed as though it were merely a figure of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Each cut has a different job: the first and second are synonyms for cutting, the third tells you to trim the word before it, and 'after' fixes the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of talking, an idiom or jargon, as in common parlance.

clue.text: Bulletin from war correspondent sadly dropped Conrad

indicators.note: sadly suggests something broken up, so the letters are rearranged
dropped says the named letters are taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: A news item tells how a war reporter sadly lost Conrad.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of CONRAD out of WAR CORRESPONDENT and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short broadcast summary of the news, i.e. a news item.

clue.text: Ability to produce and touch vegetables outside.

indicators.note: outside means the vegetables wrap around the word for touch

parts.note: greens are green leafy vegetables
to finger something is to touch it

explanation.surface: Someone who can grow crops and handle the vegetables out in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Green fingers (green thumb in the US) is the knack for making plants grow well, i.e. garden produce.

clue.text: Card-holders surprisingly led away to vergers in France!

indicators.note: surprisingly means the letters end up in an unexpected order
away means the named letters are taken out of the fodder

explanation.surface: People holding cards are led off to meet church officials in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vergers' looks like the English church officials, but it is the French word verger, a fruit garden.
explanation.definitionFit: In French verger means an orchard, so vergers are fruit-tree plantations.

clue.text: Get grime out of the mixer one's found in the kitchen

indicators.note: coming out of a mixer, the letters have been blended into a new order

explanation.surface: Cleaning grime off the food mixer, a gadget in every kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg timer, a small sand glass, is a kitchen gadget for timing boiled eggs.

clue.text: Capital way in which kings' representatives negotiate, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are spoken, giving the sound of the answer

parts.note: regents rule in place of a monarch; to treat is to negotiate terms, as in treat with the enemy

explanation.surface: A street in the capital where royal deputies conduct their negotiations.
explanation.definitionFit: Regent Street is a major shopping thoroughfare in central London, the capital.

clue.text: Discharge the French dandy for a dropped catch, maybe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... a gun or firework is to discharge it
second meaning: in cricket a batsman given a ... has been dropped by a fielder

explanation.walkthrough: Split as LE TOFF it whimsically reads as the French for the dandy, which is how 'the French dandy' sits in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-off is an escape from punishment or dismissal, like a reprieve when a fielder fumbles.

clue.text: Unaccompanied artist holds on

indicators.note: holds means the painter's name contains the next word

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was a 17th-century portrait painter at the English court

explanation.surface: A solitary painter keeps going on his own.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonely here means alone, solitary, without companions.

clue.text: Trouble that's encountered in the jacuzzi

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to be in trouble
second meaning: literally the heated water of a hot tub

explanation.definitionFit: Hot water is the idiom for difficulty or disgrace, and literally what fills a hot tub.

clue.text: Do without — selfishly?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to go without or give up
second meaning, read as two words: acting for one's own ego

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading, split 3-3 into FOR EGO.
explanation.definitionFit: To forego something is to abstain from it or sacrifice it, a variant spelling of forgo.

clue.text: Fielder brings up drink

indicators.note: in a down answer brings up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Pils is short for Pilsner lager

explanation.surface: A cricketer brings drinks out onto the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Slip is a cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper, and the fielder stationed there.

clue.text: Rough time outside major city

indicators.note: only the outside of the phrase rough time is kept, its inner letters falling away

parts.note: the phrase as written, keeping its first two and last two letters

explanation.surface: Having a hard time on the outskirts of a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'major' looks like part of the wordplay, but the definition is the phrase major city; RO and ME are the outer letters of Rough and time.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome is the Italian capital, one of the great cities of Europe.

clue.text: Get hold of wine — as stated, "a bit of body"

parts.note: to collar someone is to seize or grab them

indicators.note: as stated means as spoken, so the wine's name gives its sound

parts.note: Beaune is a Burgundy wine, named after its town in France

explanation.surface: An instruction to grab some wine, with a quoted aside about part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The collarbone, or clavicle, is a bone of the shoulder, so one part of the skeleton.

clue.text: Dried-up burn, you say

indicators.note: you say signals speech, so the word for burn gives the sound

parts.note: to sear is to scorch or burn

explanation.surface: A parched scorch mark, mentioned in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sere is a literary word for withered or parched, as of dry vegetation.

clue.text: TV host is good man, English writer, capturing hearts with fine lines.

parts.note: St, saint, a good man

indicators.note: capturing means the pen holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts
F is the pencil grade abbreviation for fine
RY, railway, means lines

explanation.surface: A television presenter described as a virtuous English author who wins hearts with his fine words.
explanation.walkthrough: Railway lines give RY. Stephen Fry is a British actor, writer and presenter of the quiz show QI.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Fry hosted the panel game QI on British television for years, a celebrity presenter.
